doc.title: Dianne Reeves interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, October 13, 2001

title: Music as salvation and performance as meditation
summary: She says music saved her life, a backdrop to the Civil Rights movement and Vietnam, and performance is spiritual for her.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Your concert tonight I thought was absolutely fabulous.

From many, many standpoints. From the variety of the songs that you sang and from the energy level that each song reached, which I thought was scintillating. I wanted to ask you where or how did you come by such conceptual strength?

Well without even going into great detail, the music saved my life. And I know growing up the music that I would listen to was really a backdrop for the Civil Rights movement, for the Vietnam War, the music was full of hope and brotherhood and positivity on all levels, not just songs that had political or social meanings but also about how men felt about women, vice versa, all of it was very, very beautiful. And I needed to hear all of those things. For me I think performance is more like meditation than it is giving a performance. It’s a spiritual place for me. So I just want to make sure a lot of times that the words that I sing about or the things that I sing about are things that I really, really believe in my soul that are really, really a part of who I am. And I think a lot of that is really what kind of shapes the music, the concept, my approach.
